title: The Tale of Zayn al-Asnam
summary: Prince Zayn al-Asnam of Basra inherited from his father vast subterranean vaults beneath his palace, wherein stood eight colossal statues...
full_text:
Prince Zayn al-Asnam of Basra inherited from his father vast subterranean vaults beneath his palace, wherein stood eight colossal statues carved of solid gold, each studded with rubies. Upon the ninth pedestal was inscribed an ancient riddle: 'Search the world for the Ninth Statue, whose value surpasses all the eight of gold!'

Guided by an ancient spirit, Prince Zayn traveled across enchanted seas to the Isle of the King of the Jinns. The King gave him a magical silver mirror, saying: 'The Ninth Statue is a living maiden whose heart is pure, whose speech is modest, and whose character is untainted by vanity or deceit. When you hold this mirror before her, if the glass remains clear as crystal, you have found the jewel.'

Zayn searched through Baghdad, Cairo, and Damascus. Every proud maiden who looked in the mirror caused the glass to turn cloudy with vain thoughts.

Finally, in a modest home in Baghdad, he met the daughter of a humble scholar. When she looked into the mirror, the silver glass shone with blinding, crystal radiance!

Zayn brought her to his palace. When she stepped onto the ninth pedestal, the King of the Jinns appeared in glory, proclaiming:

'Behold, Zayn al-Asnam! The eight golden statues are mere metal; but a virtuous, loving, and noble wife is the true ninth treasure of creation, worth more than all the gold mines of the earth!' Zayn married her in joy, ruling his realm in wisdom.
moral: A companion endowed with modesty, virtue, and character is richer than all the golden statues of the world.
